messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide to generate a **RESTful API request** for the *“get information of device connector versions”* API in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**.  
I’ve broken it down into three main sections:

| Section | What you’ll learn |
|---------|-------------------|
| 1️⃣ Dashboard UI | How to locate the API Explorer and the specific API |
| 2️⃣ Build the Request | Setting headers, query parameters, and authentication |
| 3️⃣ Execute & Inspect | Running the request, viewing the response, and exporting the call |

---

## 1️⃣ Dashboard UI – Find the API

| Step | Action | Screenshot (if available) |
|------|--------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Log in** to your Nexus Dashboard instance (https://<your‑dashboard‑url>/). |  |
| 2 | In the left‑hand navigation pane, click **Developer** → **API Explorer**. |  |
| 3 | In the API Explorer, you’ll see a list of API groups. Expand **Device Management** (or the group that contains device‑connector APIs). |  |
| 4 | Locate the API named **Get Device Connector Versions** (or similar). Click on it to open the detailed view. |  |

> **Tip:** If you can’t find the API, use the search bar at the top of the API Explorer and type “device connector versions”.

---

## 2️⃣ Build the Request – Set up everything you need

### 2.1 Endpoint & Method

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| **HTTP Method** | `GET` |
| **Endpoint** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` (the exact path may vary; check the API Explorer for the full URL) |

> **Note:** The API Explorer will display the full URL, including the base domain (`https://<your‑dashboard‑url>/api/v1/...`). Copy that URL for later use.

### 2.2 Headers

| Header | Value | Why it matters |
|--------|-------|----------------|
| `Accept` | `application/json` | Ensures you receive JSON output. |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Required for POST/PUT; optional for GET but harmless. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` | **Authentication** – you’ll need a valid JWT or OAuth token. |

> **Getting the token**:  
> 1. Go to **User Settings** → **API Tokens**.  
> 2. Click **Generate Token** (or use an existing one).  
> 3. Copy the token and paste it into the `Authorization` header as shown above.

### 2.3 Query Parameters (Optional)

| Parameter | Example | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `format` | `json` | Explicitly request JSON format (often default). |
| `limit` | `100` | Limit the number of results returned. |
| `offset` | `0` | Pagination offset. |

> **Tip:** The API Explorer will list all available query parameters. Add them by clicking the “+” icon next to each parameter.

### 2.4 Request Body

> For a `GET` request, you typically **don’t** send a body.  
> If the API requires a body (unlikely for a “get” operation), the API Explorer will show a sample JSON payload. Copy it into the **Body** tab.

---

## 3️⃣ Execute & Inspect – Run the call and see the results

### 3.1 Run the Request

| Action | Where to click |
|--------|----------------|
| **Execute** | Click the **Execute** button (usually a green play icon) in the top right corner of the API Explorer. |

> The request will be sent immediately. You’ll see a spinner while it’s processing.

### 3.2 View the Response

| Panel | What you’ll see |
|-------|-----------------|
| **Response Status** | e.g., `200 OK` |
| **Response Headers** | `Content-Type`, `Date`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, etc. |
| **Response Body** | Pretty‑printed JSON (or raw text). |
| **Response Time** | How long the request took. |
| **Response Size** | Size of the payload. |

> **Common status codes**:  
> - `200 OK` – Success.  
> - `401 Unauthorized` – Token missing/invalid.  
> - `403 Forbidden` – Insufficient permissions.  
> - `404 Not Found` – Wrong endpoint.  
> - `500 Internal Server Error` – Backend issue.

### 3.3 Export / Copy the Call

| Feature | How to use |
|---------|------------|
| **Copy cURL** | Click the **Copy cURL** button (usually a clipboard icon). Paste it into your terminal to run the same request via `curl`. |
| **Generate Code Snippet** | Click the **Generate Code** button. Choose your preferred language (Python, JavaScript, Java, etc.) and copy the snippet. |
| **Export to Postman** | Click the **Export** button → **Postman Collection**. Import the collection into Postman for further testing. |

---

## Quick Reference – cURL Example

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://<your‑dashboard‑url>/api/v1/device-connector/versions?format=json&limit=100" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your‑token>"
```

Replace `<your‑dashboard‑url>` and `<your‑token>` with your actual values.

---

## Troubleshooting Checklist

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Token expired or missing | Regenerate token or add it to the header |
| **403 Forbidden** | User lacks permission | Check role/permissions in **User Settings** |
| **404 Not Found** | Wrong endpoint | Verify the URL in the API Explorer |
| **500 Internal Server Error** | Backend issue | Contact support or retry later |
| **No response** | Network issue | Check connectivity, firewall rules |

---

## Next Steps

1. **Save the request** in the API Explorer for future use.  
2. **Add filters** (e.g., `status=active`) to narrow down results.  
3. **Schedule automated calls** using the **Scheduler** feature (if available).  
4. **Integrate** the API call into your own scripts or monitoring dashboards.

---

### Need more help?

- **Documentation**: Visit the official Cisco Nexus Dashboard API docs (https://<your‑dashboard‑url>/docs/api).  
- **Community**: Join the Cisco DevNet community (https://developer.cisco.com/) and ask questions in the Nexus Dashboard forum.  
- **Support**: Open a ticket with Cisco TAC if you encounter persistent issues.

Happy querying!
